extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, peer reviewers, journal editors and other stakeholders preparing or evaluating health research reports
extracted.subtask_description: A curated library/index of reporting guidelines and checklists for designing, conducting, and transparently reporting health-related research across many study designs (randomised trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, diagnostic accuracy, protocols, case reports, preclinical/animal studies, qualitative research, economic evaluations, AI studies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a reporting guideline?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the purpose and nature of reporting guidelines: tools to enhance the quality and transparency of health research reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides context on why reporting guidelines exist and how they should be used by authors, reviewers, and editors; points users toward the Library for specific guideline checklists and explanation documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT (randomised trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred Reporting Items for Randomised Trials — guidance and checklist for reporting randomized controlled trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes core CONSORT 2010 items and numerous CONSORT extensions (e.g., cluster trials, adaptive designs, nonpharmacologic treatments, abstracts, noninferiority/equivalence, moxibustion, acupuncture, social and psychological interventions, dose-finding extensions, Chinese herbal medicine extensions, etc.) with explanation and elaboration documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT (trial protocols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials — checklist for content of clinical trial protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers standard protocol items and SPIRIT extensions (e.g., SPIRIT-AI, SPIRIT-TCM, SPIRIT-DEFINE dose-finding) with explanation documents to help protocol authors include essential items.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA (systematic reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses — checklist and explanation for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes PRISMA 2020 and many PRISMA extensions (e.g., PRISMA-ScR for scoping reviews, PRISMA-DTA for diagnostic test accuracy, PRISMA-LSR for living SRs, PRISMA for acupuncture/Chinese herbal medicines, PRISMA for abstracts, PRISMA-CI, PRISMA-Equity) and explanation materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE (observational studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology — guidance for cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes STROBE extensions (e.g., STROBE-MR for Mendelian randomization, STROBE-Vet) and related topic-specific guidance for reporting observational data and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD (diagnostic accuracy studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies — essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes STARD 2015 and subject-specific applications (e.g., STARD for Abstracts) and extensions relevant to diagnostic test reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD (prediction model studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis — checklist for development and validation of prediction models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers items to report model development, validation and performance; includes TRIPOD-Cluster and related guidance for clustered data.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE (case reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAse REport guidelines — checklist for transparent reporting of case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes CARE extensions (e.g., CARE-DN for dry needling, CARE-radiology) and templates to help authors present complete case information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE (animal pre-clinical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments — guidelines to improve reporting of animal studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides minimum information items to enhance reproducibility and transparency in animal research reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE (quality improvement studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for QUality Improvement Reporting Excellence — guidelines for reporting quality improvement studies in healthcare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SQUIRE 2.0 provides a framework for structuring reports of improvement initiatives, including context, interventions, measures, and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS (economic evaluations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards — guidance for reporting economic evaluations of health interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes CHEERS 2022 update and extensions (e.g., CHEERS-AI, CHEERS-VOI) with items for transparently reporting model-based and trial-based cost-effectiveness analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE / RIGHT (clinical practice guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIGHT and AGREE reporting/checklist tools for developing and reporting trustworthy clinical practice guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIGHT: Reporting Tool for Practice Guidelines; AGREE Reporting Checklist: guidance to improve reporting of guideline processes, interpretation and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: COREQ / SRQR (qualitative research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ) and Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research (SRQR) — checklists for interviews, focus groups and other qualitative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COREQ is a 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups; SRQR provides standards across qualitative study types to improve transparency and methodological reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE-like / preclinical reporting and laboratory standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and checklists addressing reporting of preclinical/laboratory experiments, measurement standards and reproducibility (e.g., reporting of irradiation dosimetry, animal fecal transplantation protocols, laboratory light exposure, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic-specific recommendations aim to standardize methods description, outcome measurement, and experimental conditions to enhance replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPLE/IMAGE/AI-specific guidance (AI and ML studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple guidelines for reporting studies involving artificial intelligence, machine learning, and imaging (e.g., CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, CLAIM, MINIMAR, PRIDE, TRIPOD-LLM, DEAL, CLIX-M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover model development, validation, explainability, datasets, evaluation metrics, clinical integration, and reporting of AI-specific methodological details and ethics/COI considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidance for diagnostic/prognostic model and prediction research (extensions and specialized checklists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized checklists and consolidated guidance for prediction model reporting, including clustered data and systematic reviews of prediction models (e.g., TRIPOD-Cluster, TRIPOD-SRMA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on model transparency (predictors, outcome definitions), validation, performance measures, and data handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reporting trial protocols and amendments (extensions and targeted guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance documents for reporting trial protocols and changes (e.g., SPIRIT extensions, CONSERVE for modified trials during COVID-19, CONSORT-DEFINE for dose-finding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clear documentation of planned methods, adaptations, interim analyses, and reporting of deviations from protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reporting harms, adverse events and safety data
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized guidance on reporting adverse events, safety outcomes, and adjudication committees, including pharmacovigilance disproportion analyses and adverse event report publication standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide minimum datasets, denominators, and clarity on event definitions and ascertainment to allow accurate interpretation of harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting clinical trial statistical analysis and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and checklists for statistical reporting (e.g., SAMPL guidelines, Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines, guidance on subgroup analyses, handling missing data and multiple imputation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommendations for transparent presentation of analytic choices, model assumptions, handling of multiplicity, and effect estimation with confidence/credibility intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting imaging, electrophysiology and time-series analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Domain-specific reporting checklists and recommendations for neuroimaging, EEG/EEG-biomarker, heart rate variability, and other measurement-rich fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address acquisition parameters, preprocessing, analysis pipelines, statistical corrections, and data sharing to improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting surveys, e-surveys and field studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists and best-practice guidance for survey research and web-based surveys (e.g., CHERRIES), including question development, sampling, response rates and data handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages transparent reporting of sampling frames, recruitment, instrument development, and response biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting implementation, complex interventions and mixed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists and frameworks for reporting complex interventions, implementation research, mixed methods, scoping reviews and realist syntheses (e.g., RAMESES, GUIDED, TIDieR, TIDieR-Rehab, TIDieR-telehealth, SWiM, PRISMA-ScR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on intervention description (TIDieR), implementation context, process evaluation, and transparent methods for mixed and realist approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reporting consensus, Delphi and guideline-development processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists for reporting consensus methods, Delphi studies and development of reporting items (e.g., AC_CORD, CREDES, RIGHT-Ad@pt, REPORT-PFP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how participants were selected, rounds conducted, consensus thresholds used, and how items were generated and validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting participant- and public-involvement, equity, and social accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools and checklists for reporting patient and public involvement (GRIPP2), equity-focused reporting (PRISMA-Equity, CONSORT-Equity), intersectional analysis, social accountability and community-engaged research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage documentation of stakeholder roles, recruitment, representativeness, and considerations of equity and intersectionality in methods and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting laboratory methods, reagents and resources (RRID / resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for uniquely identifying resources and reporting materials and reagents (Resource Identification Initiative, RRID) to improve reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request authors to provide unique identifiers for antibodies, software, datasets and other resources and describe provenance and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting ethics, conflicts of interest and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and checklists for declaring conflicts of interest, funding sources, and ethical approvals (e.g., RIGHT-COI and Good Publication Practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes transparent disclosure of financial and nonfinancial interests, funder roles, and ethical oversight details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting in specialist clinical areas and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A large number of specialty- and procedure-specific reporting standards (e.g., spinal cord stimulation REPORT-SCS, endovascular repair TEVAR, paediatric ureteroscopy P-URS, many surgical and imaging reporting standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each specialty checklist provides domain-specific minimum reporting items for study methods, procedure descriptions, outcomes and follow-up relevant to that field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting AI explainability and clinical decision support evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists and evaluation frameworks for explainability and evaluation of AI tools in clinical settings (e.g., CLIX-M, DECIDE-AI, ELEVATE-GenAI, GAMER Statement, MINIMAR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address evaluation metrics, human factors, explainability, clinical workflow integration and validation in real-world settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on how to write a guideline or reporting guideline development
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and proposals for manuscript templates and methods to create trustworthy guidelines and reporting statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes methods for consensus development, public consultation, piloting and explanation/elaboration documents to support guideline uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library index — searchable catalogue of reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Library itself: a searchable, indexed list of reporting guidelines and checklists (most recently added records displayed first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can search or browse guidelines by study type, specialty or topic; pages typically link to the guideline statement, checklists, explanation & elaboration and translations when available. The Library lists hundreds of individual reporting statements and extensions across study designs, topics and specialties.
